quests.hint: Email subject line: 'Meeting Moved — Please See New Time Below.' The organizer needs a word for arranging something for a different time.
quests.explanation: RE- + SCHEDULE = RESCHEDULE, to schedule something again for a different time. This is one of the most common words in workplace email.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this workplace situation?

quests.hint: Email line: 'Please see the file attached below for the full budget breakdown.' What do you call the file itself?
quests.explanation: ATTACHMENT is ATTACH + -MENT, the noun naming a file or item joined to an email or document.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: Terms and conditions: 'Deposits can be returned in full if you cancel within 48 hours.' Which word describes a deposit like this?
quests.explanation: REFUNDABLE is REFUND + -ABLE, capable of being paid back.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A drink menu clearly separates two lists: 'Beer & Wine' on one side, and 'Mocktails' on the other, containing zero percent alcohol.
quests.explanation: NON- + ALCOHOLIC = NONALCOHOLIC, containing no alcohol. This is the same formal, label-style negation you've seen before with words like NONSMOKING and NONTOXIC.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this sign?

quests.hint: A receipt reads: 'Items may be brought back within 30 days for a full refund, with tags attached.' Which word describes items like these?
quests.explanation: RETURNABLE is RETURN + -ABLE, capable of being brought back to the store.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A sign on a staff door reads: 'Employees Only — Do Not Enter Without Permission.' Which word describes someone who enters anyway?
quests.explanation: UN- + AUTHORIZED = UNAUTHORIZED, not given official permission. NON- would sound overly formal and unnatural here — English speakers say 'unauthorized entry,' not 'nonauthorized entry.'
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this sign?

quests.hint: A university email reads: 'The window to sign up for fall classes closes this Friday at midnight.' What's the formal word for signing up like this?
quests.explanation: REGISTRATION is REGISTER + -TION, with a spelling shift, the formal process of signing up or enrolling.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A syllabus states: 'Ten percent of your grade depends on speaking up and contributing during class discussions.' What's this graded category called?
quests.explanation: PARTICIPATION is PARTICIPATE + -TION, the act of taking part in something.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A financial aid letter reads: 'Congratulations — your tuition for next year has been fully covered based on your grades.' What's the name for this kind of award?
quests.explanation: SCHOLARSHIP is SCHOLAR + -SHIP, financial support awarded to a student, or more broadly, the state of being a serious student.
quests.meaningBreakdown: SCHOLAR (root) + SHIP (suffix, forms a noun of state/relationship)
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A notification reads: 'You will no longer see posts from this account in your feed.' Which prefix fits the action that caused this?
quests.explanation: UN- + FOLLOW = UNFOLLOW, to stop following someone's account, reversing the original action of following them.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A caption reads: 'Sharing this again because it deserves way more views than it got the first time.' Which word names this action?
quests.explanation: REPOST is RE- + POST, to post something again, usually content someone else originally shared.
quests.instruction: Pick the prefix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: The bottom of a newsletter email reads: 'Click here to stop receiving these emails.' Which prefix names this action?
quests.explanation: UN- + SUBSCRIBE = UNSUBSCRIBE, to cancel a subscription. DIS- doesn't attach to SUBSCRIBE in standard English — 'dissubscribe' isn't how this idea is expressed.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A news article reads: 'Witnesses praised the firefighter's selfless bravery in running back into the building to save the child.' What's the name for behavior like this?
quests.explanation: -ISM names a belief, practice, or characteristic behavior. HERO + -ISM = HEROISM, heroic behavior or the quality of being heroic.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A review states: 'The plot dragged in the middle, and several reviewers pointed out weak pacing as the movie's biggest flaw.' What do you call feedback like this?
quests.explanation: CRITICISM is CRITIC + -ISM, the act of pointing out flaws or evaluating something's quality.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A coach tells the team: 'Even after three losses, I still believe next season will be our best yet.' What's the general belief this attitude reflects?
quests.explanation: -ISM forms OPTIMISM from the root OPTIM- ('best'), the belief that things will generally turn out well. -IST would instead name the person who holds this belief (an OPTIMIST), not the belief itself.
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A high school course description reads: 'Students will study cells, genetics, and the diversity of living organisms.' What's the name of this subject?
quests.explanation: -LOGY means 'the study of.' BIO ('life') + -LOGY = BIOLOGY, the study of living things.
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A university department focuses on how people think, feel, and behave, and why.
quests.explanation: PSYCHOLOGY is PSYCHO- ('mind') + -LOGY, the study of the mind and behavior.
quests.instruction: Pick the prefix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A field trip takes students to a canyon to examine rock layers formed over millions of years.
quests.explanation: -LOGY forms GEOLOGY from GEO- ('earth'), the study of the Earth's physical structure. You've already met the person who studies this — a GEOLOGIST — built from the same root with -IST instead.
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A checklist reminder pops up on your phone: 'Confirm your passport and boarding pass are both in your bag before leaving for the airport.' Which prefix fits this action?
quests.explanation: RE- + CHECK = RECHECK, to check something again to be sure, especially before an important trip.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A budget airline's ticket policy reads: 'Once purchased, this fare cannot be returned or exchanged for cash under any circumstances.' What's the word for a ticket like this?
quests.explanation: NONREFUNDABLE stacks NON- ('not') onto REFUNDABLE, itself REFUND + -ABLE, meaning not capable of being refunded.
quests.instruction: Pick the prefix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: After a strict airline weight check, a traveler has to take everything out of their suitcase and redo it more carefully.
quests.explanation: RE- + PACK = REPACK, to pack again, usually to fix a problem like weight or organization. OVER- would instead describe packing too much in the first place, a different issue entirely.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: Someone who wakes up every morning expecting good things to happen, no matter what went wrong yesterday.
quests.explanation: -IST names the person who holds a belief: OPTIM- + -IST = OPTIMIST. Compare this to OPTIMISM, the belief itself, built with -ISM instead — same root, two different jobs.
quests.meaningBreakdown: OPTIM (root, 'best') + IST (suffix, 'person who holds a belief')
quests.instruction: -ISM names a belief. -IST names the person who holds it. Which fits here?

quests.hint: A news article explains how a newspaper works: reporters investigate stories, editors check facts, and photographers capture images — together, this entire profession is called ___.
quests.explanation: JOURNALISM is JOURNAL + -ISM, the profession or practice of reporting news. You already know JOURNALIST, the person who does this — same root, one suffix for the practice, another for the person.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: The person whose job is to watch new movies and write an honest review for the newspaper.
quests.explanation: Here's a useful exception: the person who does this is simply a CRITIC — English never added -IST to make 'criticist.' CRITIC itself already functions as the person-noun, while -ISM (CRITICISM) names the act of judging or the feedback given. Not every pattern is perfectly regular, and recognizing the exceptions is part of mastering real English.
quests.meaningBreakdown: CRITIC (root, already the person-noun — no added suffix)
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A TV schedule note reads: 'Missed the live game? The full match airs again tonight at 9 PM.' Which prefix names this?
quests.explanation: RE- + BROADCAST = REBROADCAST, to broadcast something again, usually a recording of an earlier live event.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A fact-checking website states: 'Before publishing, our team confirms every claim against at least two independent sources.' What's the name for this process?
quests.explanation: VERIFICATION comes from VERIFY, with a spelling shift, plus -ATION, the process of confirming something is true.
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A tech review states: 'This laptop has never crashed once in the two years I've owned it.' What's the word for a product like this?
quests.explanation: RELIABLE comes from RELY, with the Y changing to I, plus -ABLE, capable of being depended on.
quests.meaningBreakdown: RELI (root, y changes to i) + ABLE (suffix, 'capable of being')
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A university program focuses on how animals, plants, and their environments interact and depend on each other.
quests.explanation: -LOGY forms ECOLOGY from ECO- ('environment/habitat'), the study of how living things relate to their surroundings. This closes the loop on BIOLOGY, PSYCHOLOGY, and GEOLOGY from earlier — all built the same way.
quests.instruction: Review: which suffix means 'the study of'?

quests.hint: A customer service reply reads: 'We've received your complaint and will respond within 48 hours.' What's the word for confirming that a message was received?
quests.explanation: ACKNOWLEDGMENT is ACKNOWLEDGE + -MENT, with the silent E often dropping, the act of confirming that something was noticed or received.
quests.meaningBreakdown: ACKNOWLEDG (root, e dropped) + MENT (suffix, verb → noun)
quests.instruction: Pick the suffix that completes the word for this meaning.

quests.hint: A community group shares an old, outdated post claiming a local store closed down — nobody meant to lie, they just shared outdated news without checking first.
quests.explanation: MIS- ('wrongly') plus INFORM plus -ATION gives MISINFORMATION, false information spread by mistake, without intent to deceive. DISINFORMATION uses DIS- instead, specifically meaning false information spread deliberately and knowingly — a meaningful real-world distinction between an honest mistake and an intentional lie.
quests.meaningBreakdown: MIS (prefix, 'wrongly') + INFORM (root) + ATION (suffix, forms a noun)
quests.instruction: Pick the prefix that completes the word for this meaning.
